## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_editor_state(include_schema: true) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_editor_state, get_guidelines, batch_get, batch_design, snapshot_layout, get_screenshot, get_variables, export_nodes, export_html.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

---
created: 2026-07-10
title: Thread base-aware write-body merge through the shared-write path (parity with owned folders)
area: sdk
files:
  - packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts
source: Phase 72 security review (LOW / informational) + CodeRabbit parity note
---

## Problem

Phase 72 made the owned-folder write-body CAS-merge base-aware (pass `baseWriteChildren` so a
locally- or remotely-deleted `WriteChildRef` is not resurrected on a CAS-409 retry), and threaded
it through `deleteItem`, `moveItem`, `restoreFromBin`, and `permanentDeleteFromBin`. But the
shared-write module `packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts` (backing `deleteFromSharedFolder`,
`moveInSharedFolder`, etc.) has NONE of its `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` call sites passing
`baseWriteChildren` — they still use the legacy naive-union merge.

Not a Phase 72 regression (this file was not touched by Phase 72 — confirmed empty in the phase
diff), so it pre-dates this work. But it is the SAME write-chain-resurrection exposure class on the
shared-folder path: a concurrent writer's stale snapshot can resurrect a `WriteChildRef` that a
share-mutation intended to drop, potentially leaving a moved/deleted item write-capable under an
old scope. The security review flagged it explicitly as a follow-up.

## Solution

Extend the base-aware pattern to every write-body-mutating `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` call in
`shared-write.ts`: capture the pre-mutation `writeChildren` snapshot and pass it as
`baseWriteChildren` (mirroring the owned-folder fixes). Add concurrent-writer resurrection
regression coverage for the shared-write delete/move paths (the writable-shares web-e2e spec has no
concurrent-move test today). Relates to [[remove-legacy-moveinsharedfolder-sharekeys-branch]] and
the Phase 72 SC#1 base-aware merge (`registration.ts`).

export const meta = {
  name: 'triage-m4-todos',
  description: 'Classify each pending todo (resolved/not-applicable/actionable/out-of-scope) with codebase verification for M4 closeout planning',
  phases: [{ title: 'Classify', detail: 'one agent per pending todo, verified against live code' }],
}

const CLASSIFY_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['file', 'title', 'area', 'status', 'evidence', 'group', 'effort', 'confidence', 'oneLiner'],
  properties: {
    file: { type: 'string' },
    title: { type: 'string', description: 'short human title of the todo' },
    area: { type: 'string', description: 'subsystem: crypto | sdk | api | web | fuse | tee | ipns | test-infra | docs | infra | auth | search' },
    status: {
      type: 'string',
      enum: ['resolved', 'not-applicable', 'actionable', 'out-of-scope-m4'],
      description: 'resolved=already done by shipped code/phase; not-applicable=superseded/dead-code-gone/moot; actionable=real remaining M4 closeout work; out-of-scope-m4=belongs to a future milestone (M5 productivity suite: team accts, billing, alt-MFA, wallet auth, CRDT sharing, async search) or is pure infra/ops',
    },
    evidence: { type: 'string', description: '1-3 sentences of concrete evidence from the code/git that justifies the status (file:line, function present/absent, phase that closed it)' },
    group: { type: 'string', description: 'thematic grouping label for phase-planning, kebab-case, e.g. crypto-zeroization-hygiene, field-rename-canonicalization, shared-write-parity, ipns-record-hardening, fuse-hardening, node-codec-kat-parity, web-ux-followups, test-infra, dead-code-retirement, recovery-tool-v3, tee-writepath-hardening' },
    effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['S', 'M', 'L'] },
    confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
    oneLiner: { type: 'string', description: 'one-line summary of what the todo asks for' },
  },
}

const TODOS = args

phase('Classify')

const results = await parallel(TODOS.map((name) => () =>
  agent(
    `You are triaging a single pending todo for the CipherBox project to help plan M4 (Milestone 4 = "v2.0 Metadata and Sharing Refactor", Phases 61-73) closeout.

CONTEXT: M4 replaced the DB-driven share_keys model with metadata-driven read/write key-chaining (node/v3 codec), added sound read/write revocation, rotation, TEE lease-renewer, and cutover the API schema. Phases 61-73 are ALL COMPLETE and shipped. The remaining pending todos are candidates for new closeout phases (74+) OR are already resolved/moot OR belong to a FUTURE milestone (M5 = encrypted productivity suite: team accounts, billing, alternative MFA factors, ERC-1271 wallet auth, CRDT inbox sharing, async incremental search).

YOUR TASK: Read the todo file at .planning/todos/pending/${name} in the repo root (/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box). Then VERIFY against the LIVE codebase whether it is already resolved, no longer applicable, still actionable, or out-of-scope for M4.

Verification steps (do these — do not guess):
- Read the todo fully (note the 'files:', 'source:', and 'area:' frontmatter and the Problem/Solution).
- grep/read the specific files, functions, fields, or symbols the todo names. If it asks to rename X->Y, check whether X still exists or Y is already in place. If it asks to remove dead code, check whether that code is still present. If it asks to add zeroization/a helper/a test, check whether it now exists.
- Optionally check 'git log --oneline -20 -- <path>' or 'git log --oneline --all | head' for phases that may have closed it (Phases 70, 70.1, 71, 72, 73 landed AFTER many of these todos were filed).
- Decide status per the schema. Prefer 'resolved' or 'not-applicable' ONLY with concrete evidence; if unsure whether recent phases closed it, mark 'actionable' with confidence 'low' and say what you couldn't confirm.

Be terse and evidence-driven. Return the structured classification.`,
    { label: name.replace(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-/, '').replace(/\.md$/, '').slice(0, 40), phase: 'Classify', schema: CLASSIFY_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }
  )
))

return results.filter(Boolean)

export const meta = {
  name: 'triage-m4-todos',
  description: 'Classify each pending todo (resolved/not-applicable/actionable/out-of-scope) with codebase verification for M4 closeout planning',
  phases: [{ title: 'Classify', detail: 'one agent per pending todo, verified against live code' }],
}

const CLASSIFY_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['file', 'title', 'area', 'status', 'evidence', 'group', 'effort', 'confidence', 'oneLiner'],
  properties: {
    file: { type: 'string' },
    title: { type: 'string', description: 'short human title of the todo' },
    area: { type: 'string', description: 'subsystem: crypto | sdk | api | web | fuse | tee | ipns | test-infra | docs | infra | auth | search' },
    status: {
      type: 'string',
      enum: ['resolved', 'not-applicable', 'actionable', 'out-of-scope-m4'],
      description: 'resolved=already done by shipped code/phase; not-applicable=superseded/dead-code-gone/moot; actionable=real remaining M4 closeout work; out-of-scope-m4=belongs to a future milestone (M5 productivity suite: team accts, billing, alt-MFA, wallet auth, CRDT sharing, async search) or is pure infra/ops',
    },
    evidence: { type: 'string', description: '1-3 sentences of concrete evidence from the code/git that justifies the status (file:line, function present/absent, phase that closed it)' },
    group: { type: 'string', description: 'thematic grouping label for phase-planning, kebab-case, e.g. crypto-zeroization-hygiene, field-rename-canonicalization, shared-write-parity, ipns-record-hardening, fuse-hardening, node-codec-kat-parity, web-ux-followups, test-infra, dead-code-retirement, recovery-tool-v3, tee-writepath-hardening' },
    effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['S', 'M', 'L'] },
    confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
    oneLiner: { type: 'string', description: 'one-line summary of what the todo asks for' },
  },
}

const TODOS = args

phase('Classify')

const results = await parallel(TODOS.map((name) => () =>
  agent(
    `You are triaging a single pending todo for the CipherBox project to help plan M4 (Milestone 4 = "v2.0 Metadata and Sharing Refactor", Phases 61-73) closeout.

CONTEXT: M4 replaced the DB-driven share_keys model with metadata-driven read/write key-chaining (node/v3 codec), added sound read/write revocation, rotation, TEE lease-renewer, and cutover the API schema. Phases 61-73 are ALL COMPLETE and shipped. The remaining pending todos are candidates for new closeout phases (74+) OR are already resolved/moot OR belong to a FUTURE milestone (M5 = encrypted productivity suite: team accounts, billing, alternative MFA factors, ERC-1271 wallet auth, CRDT inbox sharing, async incremental search).

YOUR TASK: Read the todo file at .planning/todos/pending/${name} in the repo root (/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box). Then VERIFY against the LIVE codebase whether it is already resolved, no longer applicable, still actionable, or out-of-scope for M4.

Verification steps (do these — do not guess):
- Read the todo fully (note the 'files:', 'source:', and 'area:' frontmatter and the Problem/Solution).
- grep/read the specific files, functions, fields, or symbols the todo names. If it asks to rename X->Y, check whether X still exists or Y is already in place. If it asks to remove dead code, check whether that code is still present. If it asks to add zeroization/a helper/a test, check whether it now exists.
- Optionally check 'git log --oneline -20 -- <path>' or 'git log --oneline --all | head' for phases that may have closed it (Phases 70, 70.1, 71, 72, 73 landed AFTER many of these todos were filed).
- Decide status per the schema. Prefer 'resolved' or 'not-applicable' ONLY with concrete evidence; if unsure whether recent phases closed it, mark 'actionable' with confidence 'low' and say what you couldn't confirm.

Be terse and evidence-driven. Return the structured classification.`,
    { label: name.replace(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-/, '').replace(/\.md$/, '').slice(0, 40), phase: 'Classify', schema: CLASSIFY_SCHEMA, effort: 'medium' }
  )
))

return results.filter(Boolean)

content.text:
42 todos classified against live code. Here's the synthesis.

## Bottom line

- **3 resolved**, **1 not‑applicable**, **1 duplicate pair**, **9 out‑of‑scope for M4** → 14 to clear off the pending list.
- **28 actionable** items cluster cleanly into **5 closeout phases** (74–78), with the two revocation‑correctness clusters being the only ones that genuinely *must* land before M4 ships (they're bugs in the exact revocation guarantee M4 exists to deliver).

---

## Clear off the list now

**Resolved (retire → completed):**
| Todo | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `web-e2e-flaky-cascade-abort` | PR #593 moved Playwright to file‑level parallelism (workers=3, per‑file wallet isolation); no cascade-abort remains |
| `rotation-hardening-followups-from-pr-review` | All 6 items closed by Phase 70 + 70.1 (#598) |
| `add-permanent-delete-confirmation-dialog` | `ConfirmDialog` "cannot be undone" now gates single + batch delete. *Caveat:* prompt is unconditional, not gated on `deleteBehavior==='permanent'` — the literal D‑02 wording differentiation isn't done, but the safety gap is closed |

**Not‑applicable (verify then retire):**
- `shared-write-base-aware-merge-parity` — `shared-write.ts` publishes via fail‑closed CAS (`publishOrThrow`, throws on 409), so the naive‑union merge‑on‑409 resurrection vector *doesn't exist* on this rewritten node/v3 path. Agent confidence **medium** — worth a 5‑min confirm since the security review flagged it, but almost certainly moot.

**Duplicate:** `2026-07-03-port-recovery-tool-to-v3-vault-format` and `2026-06-29-recovery-html-vault-v3-migration` are the **same work** (recovery.html v2→v3). Merge into one todo.

**Out‑of‑scope for M4 (defer to M5 / backlog):**
- M5 features: `alternative-mfa-factor-types`, `erc-1271-contract-wallet-authentication`, `crdt-ipns-inbox-sharing`, `async-incremental-search-index`
- Infra/ops/docs: `periodic-kubo-ipfs-gc-on-staging`, `scrub-staging-ssh-host`, `web-logger-redaction-faro` (observability, Phase 30 debt)
- Orthogonal debt: `large-file-refactor-tier3-residue`, `desktop-e2e-recycle-bin-test-parity` (Phase 56 test‑infra)

---

## Proposed M4 closeout phases (28 actionable items)

**🔴 Phase 74 — Rust/FUSE Rotation‑Revocation Soundness** *(must‑ship; these are real revocation bypasses on desktop)*
- Deep scope‑exit rotation refreshes only grant‑root inode key, not intermediate parents (needs engine to surface per‑node keys, Rust+TS parity) — **L**
- `query_grants_rooted_at` no‑op de‑authorizes *all* recipients on scope‑exit rotation (re‑mint seam never wired) — **M**
- WinFsp RENAME lacks D‑15d dest‑gating + fuser ordering parity (overwrite‑rename bypass on Windows) — **S**

**🔴 Phase 75 — Cross‑Language IPNS/Node‑Codec Verification Parity** *(closes crypto verification blind spots)*
- Strict RFC3339 Validity parse in TS resolve (match Rust) — **S**
- Enforce `ValidityType==0` before treating Validity as expiry (Rust+TS) + expired/wrong‑type vectors — **M**
- Node‑codec KAT: pin `file_iv` to encoding‑unambiguous base64 (hex impl currently still passes) — **S**
- UUID acceptance‑domain parity in AAD builder (TS `uuidToBytes` vs Rust `parse_str`) — **S**

**🟡 Phase 76 — FUSE Durability + TEE Write‑Path Hardening**
- Vault‑init publish‑ordering preflight (resolve both IPNS names, fail‑closed) — **M**
- Deferred Phase 69 FUSE publish/concurrency items (retry helper, global FP‑resolve cap, Windows D‑07 node_id) — **M**
- TEE republish write‑path error handling (distinguish real DB errors from CAS‑miss) — **S**
- `renewIpnsRecord` strictly‑later‑EOL invariant + fix the tests that don't assert their branch — **S**

**🟢 Phase 77 — Crypto Hygiene + Terminology Canonicalization** *(mechanical, low‑risk; largest bucket, 11 items — splittable)*
- Zeroization: `wrapIpnsKeyForTee` bytes‑in/out, `createSubfolder` error‑path, AES‑GCM helper copies, `verify-filepointer.mts` — **4×S**
- base64 dedup: hoist `base64ToBytes` into `@cipherbox/crypto`; collapse sdk‑core/share + node/ codec copies — **3×S**
- Field renames: `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted`→`encryptedIpnsPrivateKey` (in‑memory); `encryptedIpnsKey`/`upgradedEncryptedKey`→canonical (wire) — **S + M**
- Dead code: retire SDK `ShareCallbacks`/`addShareKeysFn`; drop discarded per‑upload ECIES wrapKey — **2×S**

**🟢 Phase 78 — Recovery Tool v3 + Web UX + CI Guards**
- **recovery.html v2→v3** (offline recovery is currently *broken* for all v3 vaults; also un‑fixmes `recovery.spec.ts`) — **L**, higher priority than its bucket
- Download‑progress UX decision (`useFileDownload` is dead — wire it or delete it) — **S**
- D‑07 web/SDK boundary → ESLint/CI rule (currently manual grep only) — **S**
- Web vitest in CI + broken `ipns.service.test.ts` (test already deleted #589; CI gap remains) — **S**
- 68.2 CodeRabbit backlog (2/11 shipped; remainder = SDK perf + web a11y) — **L**

**Standalone / low‑priority:** `macos-fuse-t-cross-client-sync-invalidation` (**L**, agent confidence **low**) — this is the infra‑limited FUSE‑T cache stopgap (#560), not really a code fix. Keep parked.

---

Recommendation: sequence **74 → 75** first (revocation + crypto correctness are the actual M4 completion criteria), then 76–78 as cleanup before milestone close. 77 is a clean single "hygiene" phase but you could split zeroization/dedup from renames if you want tighter PRs.

Want me to (a) write these into `ROADMAP.md` as phases 74–78 via `/gsd-phase`, (b) retire the resolved/NA/duplicate todos, or (c) both?

---
created: 2026-07-06
title: Phase 68.2 CodeRabbit hardening backlog (cache/freshness/a11y/tests)
area: sdk
files:
  - packages/sdk/src/client.ts
  - packages/sdk/src/folder-listing.ts
  - apps/web/src/hooks/useSyncPolling.ts
  - apps/web/src/components/file-browser/FileList.tsx
  - apps/web/src/components/file-browser/SharedFileBrowser.tsx
resolves_phase: null
---

## Problem

Non-blocking hardening findings from the Phase 68.2 ship-review (CodeRabbit).
None observed in the passing e2e/unit suites; deferred rather than changing
cache/freshness semantics late in a verified-green phase. Grouped here:

## Items

1. **Owned `listingCache` invalidation on file-only mutations** (`client.ts`
   ~`resolveListingChildren`/`3613`). The shared path already invalidates
   `listingCache` on a file-only publish (`client.ts:5028`); the OWNED path
   (`replaceFile` / `restoreFileVersion` / `deleteFileVersion`) does not, so a
   cached `ResolvedChild[]` could serve stale size/modifiedAt/version. **Masked
   today** because the web forces resolve after these mutations (68.2-14/16
   `forceResolve` + `invalidateOpenFolder`), bypassing the cache — but the SDK
   cache staying stale is latent for any non-forcing consumer. Mirror the
   shared-path `listingCache.delete(ipnsName)`.

2. **`toResolvedChildView` unresolved default** (`FileList.tsx:23-36`). Falls
   back to `kind: 'folder'` when a raw child has no paired `ResolvedChild`
   (matches the historical folder-safe default; e2e nav passes because the
   store sets `children`/`rawChildren` atomically). Harden by threading an
   explicit "unresolved" state and disabling double-click nav / drag until the
   item resolves, instead of defaulting to a navigable folder.

3. **`invalidateOpenFolder` monotonicity** (`useSyncPolling.ts:39-47`). The
   poll-leg writeback re-checks folder identity but not sequence monotonicity —
   a slow await racing a newer nav re-resolve could apply older (still
   above-floor) children over newer. Add a stored-vs-resolved `sequenceNumber`
   guard before `updateFolderChildren`.

4. **`refreshSharedFolder` stale write envelope** (`client.ts:5229`). Refresh
   adopts children+sequence but leaves the write-body `publishedNode` stale, so
   a later shared write may republish an outdated write-body. Pass the freshly
   resolved `PublishedNode` into `adoptSharedFolderResult` as `publishedParent`.
   **IMPLEMENTED in Phase 73 (73-05).** A follow-up seq-consistency guard was
   ALSO added during the Phase 73 ship review (CodeRabbit Major): the two
   independent resolves (`loadFolderMetadata` result vs the separate
   `resolvePublishedNode`) are now reconciled — `publishedParent` is adopted
   only when `parentResolved.sequenceNumber >= result.sequenceNumber`, so a
   raced/older envelope can no longer seed a stale write base. Residual
   follow-up (Phase 73 crypto/security review, LOW, defense-in-depth): the
   resolve is still a raw `resolvePublishedNode`, not the ROT-07-gated variant
   the sibling read facades use (SC3). The seq guard + the in-memory
   monotonicity guard (`client.ts:5647`) + server CAS cover the realistic
   rollback vectors; the residual is full floor-gating by
   `generation`/`versionFloor`, which the share root has no parent mirror to
   source from — a non-trivial SDK change deferred to a future write-plane
   hardening pass.

5. **`ResolvedChild.sequence` safe-integer narrowing** (`folder-listing.ts:115`).
   `Number(sequenceNumber)` isn't range-checked at this site (the upstream
   gated resolve guards `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` only when `rotationHighWater` is
   configured). Validate/handle out-of-range explicitly before conversion.

6. **Shared empty-state grid a11y** (`SharedFileBrowser.tsx:810-822`). The
   empty-state div sits directly under a `rowgroup`, breaking grid semantics;
   wrap it in a `role="row"` (with a cell) or move it out of the grid.

7. **SDK test hardening** — stronger/added assertions CodeRabbit requested:
   fail-closed (`signatureVerified: false`) cases for the gated facades
   (`resolve-child-identity.test.ts`, `descend-shared-child.test.ts` — see the
   companion gating todo), assert trusted-vs-envelope generation in
   `folder-reresolve.test.ts`, and tighten the `selectEncryptionMode` assertion
   in `folder-metadata-facade.test.ts`.

8. **Double forced re-resolve on cold navigation** (`useFolderNavigation.ts`
   ~`refreshFolderListing`:68-73). The D-03 belt-and-suspenders leg runs
   `listFolder({ forceResolve })` and `ensureFolderLoaded({ forceResolve })`
   concurrently; `listFolder` also drives `ensureFolderLoaded` internally, so a
   cold nav can pay for two back-to-back IPNS resolves. **Deferred, not fixed:**
   both legs are `forceResolve` on the freshness-critical path we just hardened
   for Regression B (68.2-16) and return different shapes (`ResolvedChild[]` vs
   raw `children` + `sequenceNumber`). The clean fix is an SDK API change —
   expose the raw state + sequence from `listFolder` (or dedup the two forced
   resolves in-SDK via `reresolveInFlight`) so the web needs one call. Do NOT
   just drop `forceResolve` on the second leg — that reintroduces the stale
   `rawChildren`/`sequence` staleness Regression B fixed. Verify against
   writable-shares + shared-folder-desync e2e.

9. **Shared resolved-listing projection may fire before the SDK seed**
   (`useSharedNavigation.ts`:355-375). The display projection effect calls
   `listSharedFolder(currentShareId, [])`, which reads `sharedFolderTree`, but
   `setFolderChildren`/`setCurrentView` run before `seedActiveSharedFolder`, so
   an intermediate render could hit the "Shared folder not loaded" path and
   leave `resolvedChildren` empty. **Masked today** — the effect deps include
   `folderChildren`/`currentSequenceNumber`, which change on seed completion and
   re-fire the projection (writable-shares 29/29 + shared-folder-desync green).
   Harden by gating the effect on seed completion (or moving the seed earlier)
   so the projection only runs against a seeded tree; the reorder touches the
   delicate shared-nav seeding sequence, so validate with the shared e2e suites.

10. **Parallelize `resolveChildren`** (`folder-listing.ts`:87-127). Per-child
    resolution (`gatedResolve` + `unsealChildReadKey` + `unsealNode`) is
    sequential, so a listing over an N-child folder blocks on N serial
    IPNS+IPFS round-trips (a rename in a 100-file folder pays 100 sequential
    resolves before the mutation promise resolves). Bound with the existing
    `p-limit` (already a dep, used for `UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY`) at 3-5 concurrent,
    threaded in from `resolveListingChildren`. Preserve result ordering by input
    index, the skip-on-failure semantics, the `resolved.length < children.length`
    partial-cache guard (Greptile P1), and per-child `childReadKey` zeroing.

11. **In-flight descent can overwrite a restore** (`useSharedNavigationActions.ts`
    ~`navigateToSubfolder`/`restoreToBreadcrumbIndex`, Phase 73 Greptile P1).
    `navigateToSubfolder` pushes the parent entry then `await`s the child
    write-key derivation + `seedActiveSharedFolder`; a fast `navigateUp` /
    breadcrumb click during that await can restore the parent first, then the
    descent resumes and seeds the SDK `sharedFolderTree` with the CHILD depth
    while the UI shows the parent -- so the next shared write can publish with
    the wrong `ipnsName`/`writeKey` (data-integrity: write to the wrong folder).
    Narrow window (requires interaction during the async seed gap) and rooted in
    the pre-existing async nav-seed architecture, not the Phase 73 key-retention
    work per se, but Phase 73 widened the blast radius (wrong writeKey too, not
    just ipnsName). Fix needs an in-flight generation/cancellation token on the
    active depth so a stale descent's seed is dropped once a newer nav has run;
    deferred rather than rushing a concurrency guard at ship time. Validate with
    writable-shares + shared-folder-desync e2e (add a descend-then-immediately-up
    race case).

---
created: 2026-07-10
title: Thread base-aware write-body merge through the shared-write path (parity with owned folders)
area: sdk
files:
  - packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts
source: Phase 72 security review (LOW / informational) + CodeRabbit parity note
---

## Problem

Phase 72 made the owned-folder write-body CAS-merge base-aware (pass `baseWriteChildren` so a
locally- or remotely-deleted `WriteChildRef` is not resurrected on a CAS-409 retry), and threaded
it through `deleteItem`, `moveItem`, `restoreFromBin`, and `permanentDeleteFromBin`. But the
shared-write module `packages/sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts` (backing `deleteFromSharedFolder`,
`moveInSharedFolder`, etc.) has NONE of its `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` call sites passing
`baseWriteChildren` — they still use the legacy naive-union merge.

Not a Phase 72 regression (this file was not touched by Phase 72 — confirmed empty in the phase
diff), so it pre-dates this work. But it is the SAME write-chain-resurrection exposure class on the
shared-folder path: a concurrent writer's stale snapshot can resurrect a `WriteChildRef` that a
share-mutation intended to drop, potentially leaving a moved/deleted item write-capable under an
old scope. The security review flagged it explicitly as a follow-up.

## Solution

Extend the base-aware pattern to every write-body-mutating `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish` call in
`shared-write.ts`: capture the pre-mutation `writeChildren` snapshot and pass it as
`baseWriteChildren` (mirroring the owned-folder fixes). Add concurrent-writer resurrection
regression coverage for the shared-write delete/move paths (the writable-shares web-e2e spec has no
concurrent-move test today). Relates to [[remove-legacy-moveinsharedfolder-sharekeys-branch]] and
the Phase 72 SC#1 base-aware merge (`registration.ts`).

title: Migrate recovery.html emergency page from vault blob v2 to v3
area: web

## Problem

Phase 62 hard-cut the vault recovery blob to v3 (D-05): two-key layout
`0x03 | u16_BE(readLen) | ECIES(rootReadKey) | u16_BE(writeLen) | ECIES(rootWriteKey)`,
and deleted the v1/v2 serializers plus `encryptedRootFolderKey`.

The static emergency-recovery page `apps/web/public/recovery.html` still
implements `deserializeVaultBlobV2` and references `encryptedRootFolderKey`. It
is a standalone HTML/JS page (not TypeScript source, not imported by any phase-62
plan), so it was out of scope and the typecheck gate never saw it. Against a real
v3 vault blob it would fail to recover.

No real-world impact yet: the app is intentionally non-runnable mid-milestone

## Problem

Non-blocking hardening findings from the Phase 68.2 ship-review (CodeRabbit).
None observed in the passing e2e/unit suites; deferred rather than changing
cache/freshness semantics late in a verified-green phase. Grouped here:

## Items

1. **Owned `listingCache` invalidation on file-only mutations** (`client.ts`
   ~`resolveListingChildren`/`3613`). The shared path already invalidates
   `listingCache` on a file-only publish (`client.ts:5028`); the OWNED path
   (`replaceFile` / `restoreFileVersion` / `deleteFileVersion`) does not, so a
   cached `ResolvedChild[]` could serve stale size/modifiedAt/version. **Masked
   today** because the web forces resolve after these mutations (68.2-14/16
   `forceResolve` + `invalidateOpenFolder`), bypassing the cache — but the SDK
   cache staying stale is latent for any non-forcing consumer. Mirror the
   shared-path `listingCache.delete(ipnsName)`.

2. **`toResolvedChildView` unresolved default** (`FileList.tsx:23-36`). Falls
   back to `kind: 'folder'` when a raw child has no paired `ResolvedChild`
   (matches the historical folder-safe default; e2e nav passes because the
   store sets `children`/`rawChildren` atomically). Harden by threading an
   explicit "unresolved" state and disabling double-click nav / drag until the
   item resolves, instead of defaulting to a navigable folder.

3. **`invalidateOpenFolder` monotonicity** (`useSyncPolling.ts:39-47`). The
   poll-leg writeback re-checks folder identity but not sequence monotonicity —
   a slow await racing a newer nav re-resolve could apply older (still
   above-floor) children over newer. Add a stored-vs-resolved `sequenceNumber`
   guard before `updateFolderChildren`.

4. **`refreshSharedFolder` stale write envelope** (`client.ts:5229`). Refresh
   adopts children+sequence but leaves the write-body `publishedNode` stale, so
   a later shared write may republish an outdated write-body. Pass the freshly
   resolved `PublishedNode` into `adoptSharedFolderResult` as `publishedParent`.
   **IMPLEMENTED in Phase 73 (73-05).** A follow-up seq-consistency guard was
   ALSO added during the Phase 73 ship review (CodeRabbit Major): the two
   independent resolves (`loadFolderMetadata` result vs the separate
   `resolvePublishedNode`) are now reconciled — `publishedParent` is adopted
   only when `parentResolved.sequenceNumber >= result.sequenceNumber`, so a
   raced/older envelope can no longer seed a stale write base. Residual
   follow-up (Phase 73 crypto/security review, LOW, defense-in-depth): the
   resolve is still a raw `resolvePublishedNode`, not the ROT-07-gated variant
   the sibling read facades use (SC3). The seq guard + the in-memory
   monotonicity guard (`client.ts:5647`) + server CAS cover the realistic
   rollback vectors; the residual is full floor-gating by
   `generation`/`versionFloor`, which the share root has no parent mirror to
   source from — a non-trivial SDK change deferred to a future write-plane
   hardening pass.

5. **`ResolvedChild.sequence` safe-integer narrowing** (`folder-listing.ts:115`).
   `Number(sequenceNumber)` isn't range-checked at this site (the upstream
   gated resolve guards `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` only when `rotationHighWater` is
   configured). Validate/handle out-of-range explicitly before conversion.

6. **Shared empty-state grid a11y** (`SharedFileBrowser.tsx:810-822`). The
   empty-state div sits directly under a `rowgroup`, breaking grid semantics;
   wrap it in a `role="row"` (with a cell) or move it out of the grid.

7. **SDK test hardening** — stronger/added assertions CodeRabbit requested:
   fail-closed (`signatureVerified: false`) cases for the gated facades
   (`resolve-child-identity.test.ts`, `descend-shared-child.test.ts` — see the
   companion gating todo), assert trusted-vs-envelope generation in
   `folder-reresolve.test.ts`, and tighten the `selectEncryptionMode` assertion
   in `folder-metadata-facade.test.ts`.

8. **Double forced re-resolve on cold navigation** (`useFolderNavigation.ts`
   ~`refreshFolderListing`:68-73). The D-03 belt-and-suspenders leg runs
   `listFolder({ forceResolve })` and `ensureFolderLoaded({ forceResolve })`
   concurrently; `listFolder` also drives `ensureFolderLoaded` internally, so a
   cold nav can pay for two back-to-back IPNS resolves. **Deferred, not fixed:**
   both legs are `forceResolve` on the freshness-critical path we just hardened
   for Regression B (68.2-16) and return different shapes (`ResolvedChild[]` vs
   raw `children` + `sequenceNumber`). The clean fix is an SDK API change —
   expose the raw state + sequence from `listFolder` (or dedup the two forced
   resolves in-SDK via `reresolveInFlight`) so the web needs one call. Do NOT
   just drop `forceResolve` on the second leg — that reintroduces the stale
   `rawChildren`/`sequence` staleness Regression B fixed. Verify against
   writable-shares + shared-folder-desync e2e.

9. **Shared resolved-listing projection may fire before the SDK seed**
   (`useSharedNavigation.ts`:355-375). The display projection effect calls
   `listSharedFolder(currentShareId, [])`, which reads `sharedFolderTree`, but
   `setFolderChildren`/`setCurrentView` run before `seedActiveSharedFolder`, so
   an intermediate render could hit the "Shared folder not loaded" path and
   leave `resolvedChildren` empty. **Masked today** — the effect deps include
   `folderChildren`/`currentSequenceNumber`, which change on seed completion and
   re-fire the projection (writable-shares 29/29 + shared-folder-desync green).
   Harden by gating the effect on seed completion (or moving the seed earlier)
   so the projection only runs against a seeded tree; the reorder touches the
   delicate shared-nav seeding sequence, so validate with the shared e2e suites.

10. **Parallelize `resolveChildren`** (`folder-listing.ts`:87-127). Per-child
    resolution (`gatedResolve` + `unsealChildReadKey` + `unsealNode`) is
    sequential, so a listing over an N-child folder blocks on N serial
    IPNS+IPFS round-trips (a rename in a 100-file folder pays 100 sequential
    resolves before the mutation promise resolves). Bound with the existing
    `p-limit` (already a dep, used for `UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY`) at 3-5 concurrent,
    threaded in from `resolveListingChildren`. Preserve result ordering by input
    index, the skip-on-failure semantics, the `resolved.length < children.length`
    partial-cache guard (Greptile P1), and per-child `childReadKey` zeroing.

11. **In-flight descent can overwrite a restore** (`useSharedNavigationActions.ts`
    ~`navigateToSubfolder`/`restoreToBreadcrumbIndex`, Phase 73 Greptile P1).
    `navigateToSubfolder` pushes the parent entry then `await`s the child
    write-key derivation + `seedActiveSharedFolder`; a fast `navigateUp` /
    breadcrumb click during that await can restore the parent first, then the
    descent resumes and seeds the SDK `sharedFolderTree` with the CHILD depth
    while the UI shows the parent -- so the next shared write can publish with
    the wrong `ipnsName`/`writeKey` (data-integrity: write to the wrong folder).
    Narrow window (requires interaction during the async seed gap) and rooted in
    the pre-existing async nav-seed architecture, not the Phase 73 key-retention
    work per se, but Phase 73 widened the blast radius (wrong writeKey too, not
    just ipnsName). Fix needs an in-flight generation/cancellation token on the
    active depth so a stale descent's seed is dropped once a newer nav has run;
    deferred rather than rushing a concurrency guard at ship time. Validate with
    writable-shares + shared-folder-desync e2e (add a descend-then-immediately-up
    race case).

   (`client.ts:3966-3968`), mirroring the shared path. Original concern (cached
   `ResolvedChild[]` serving stale size/modifiedAt/version, masked only by the
   web `forceResolve`) is closed.

2. **`toResolvedChildView` unresolved default** (`FileList.tsx:23-36`). Falls
   back to `kind: 'folder'` when a raw child has no paired `ResolvedChild`
   (matches the historical folder-safe default; e2e nav passes because the
   store sets `children`/`rawChildren` atomically). Harden by threading an
   explicit "unresolved" state and disabling double-click nav / drag until the
   item resolves, instead of defaulting to a navigable folder.

3. **`invalidateOpenFolder` monotonicity** (`useSyncPolling.ts:39-47`). The
   poll-leg writeback re-checks folder identity but not sequence monotonicity —
   a slow await racing a newer nav re-resolve could apply older (still
   above-floor) children over newer. Add a stored-vs-resolved `sequenceNumber`
   guard before `updateFolderChildren`.

4. **✅ RESOLVED (Phase 73, 73-05; residual ROT-07 gating deferred).**
   **`refreshSharedFolder` stale write envelope** (`client.ts`). Refresh
   adopts children+sequence but leaves the write-body `publishedNode` stale, so
   a later shared write may republish an outdated write-body. Pass the freshly
   resolved `PublishedNode` into `adoptSharedFolderResult` as `publishedParent`.
   **IMPLEMENTED in Phase 73 (73-05).** A follow-up seq-consistency guard was
   ALSO added during the Phase 73 ship review (CodeRabbit Major): the two
   independent resolves (`loadFolderMetadata` result vs the separate
   `resolvePublishedNode`) are now reconciled — `publishedParent` is adopted
   only when `parentResolved.sequenceNumber >= result.sequenceNumber`, so a
   raced/older envelope can no longer seed a stale write base. Residual
   follow-up (Phase 73 crypto/security review, LOW, defense-in-depth): the
   resolve is still a raw `resolvePublishedNode`, not the ROT-07-gated variant
   the sibling read facades use (SC3). The seq guard + the in-memory
   monotonicity guard (`client.ts:5647`) + server CAS cover the realistic
   rollback vectors; the residual is full floor-gating by
   `generation`/`versionFloor`, which the share root has no parent mirror to
   source from — a non-trivial SDK change deferred to a future write-plane
   hardening pass.

5. **`ResolvedChild.sequence` safe-integer narrowing** (`folder-listing.ts:115`).
   `Number(sequenceNumber)` isn't range-checked at this site (the upstream
   gated resolve guards `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` only when `rotationHighWater` is
   configured). Validate/handle out-of-range explicitly before conversion.

6. **Shared empty-state grid a11y** (`SharedFileBrowser.tsx:810-822`). The
   empty-state div sits directly under a `rowgroup`, breaking grid semantics;
   wrap it in a `role="row"` (with a cell) or move it out of the grid.

7. **SDK test hardening** — stronger/added assertions CodeRabbit requested:
   fail-closed (`signatureVerified: false`) cases for the gated facades
   (`resolve-child-identity.test.ts`, `descend-shared-child.test.ts` — see the
   companion gating todo), assert trusted-vs-envelope generation in
   `folder-reresolve.test.ts`, and tighten the `selectEncryptionMode` assertion
   in `folder-metadata-facade.test.ts`.

8. **Double forced re-resolve on cold navigation** (`useFolderNavigation.ts`
   ~`refreshFolderListing`:68-73). The D-03 belt-and-suspenders leg runs
   `listFolder({ forceResolve })` and `ensureFolderLoaded({ forceResolve })`
   concurrently; `listFolder` also drives `ensureFolderLoaded` internally, so a
   cold nav can pay for two back-to-back IPNS resolves. **Deferred, not fixed:**
   both legs are `forceResolve` on the freshness-critical path we just hardened
   for Regression B (68.2-16) and return different shapes (`ResolvedChild[]` vs
   raw `children` + `sequenceNumber`). The clean fix is an SDK API change —
   expose the raw state + sequence from `listFolder` (or dedup the two forced
   resolves in-SDK via `reresolveInFlight`) so the web needs one call. Do NOT
   just drop `forceResolve` on the second leg — that reintroduces the stale
   `rawChildren`/`sequence` staleness Regression B fixed. Verify against
   writable-shares + shared-folder-desync e2e.

9. **Shared resolved-listing projection may fire before the SDK seed**
   (`useSharedNavigation.ts`:355-375). The display projection effect calls
   `listSharedFolder(currentShareId, [])`, which reads `sharedFolderTree`, but
   `setFolderChildren`/`setCurrentView` run before `seedActiveSharedFolder`, so
   an intermediate render could hit the "Shared folder not loaded" path and
   leave `resolvedChildren` empty. **Masked today** — the effect deps include
   `folderChildren`/`currentSequenceNumber`, which change on seed completion and
   re-fire the projection (writable-shares 29/29 + shared-folder-desync green).
   Harden by gating the effect on seed completion (or moving the seed earlier)
   so the projection only runs against a seeded tree; the reorder touches the
   delicate shared-nav seeding sequence, so validate with the shared e2e suites.

10. **Parallelize `resolveChildren`** (`folder-listing.ts`:87-127). Per-child
    resolution (`gatedResolve` + `unsealChildReadKey` + `unsealNode`) is
    sequential, so a listing over an N-child folder blocks on N serial
    IPNS+IPFS round-trips (a rename in a 100-file folder pays 100 sequential
    resolves before the mutation promise resolves). Bound with the existing
    `p-limit` (already a dep, used for `UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY`) at 3-5 concurrent,
    threaded in from `resolveListingChildren`. Preserve result ordering by input
    index, the skip-on-failure semantics, the `resolved.length < children.length`
    partial-cache guard (Greptile P1), and per-child `childReadKey` zeroing.

11. **In-flight descent can overwrite a restore** (`useSharedNavigationActions.ts`
    ~`navigateToSubfolder`/`restoreToBreadcrumbIndex`, Phase 73 Greptile P1).
    `navigateToSubfolder` pushes the parent entry then `await`s the child
    write-key derivation + `seedActiveSharedFolder`; a fast `navigateUp` /
    breadcrumb click during that await can restore the parent first, then the
    descent resumes and seeds the SDK `sharedFolderTree` with the CHILD depth
    while the UI shows the parent -- so the next shared write can publish with
    the wrong `ipnsName`/`writeKey` (data-integrity: write to the wrong folder).
    Narrow window (requires interaction during the async seed gap) and rooted in
    the pre-existing async nav-seed architecture, not the Phase 73 key-retention
    work per se, but Phase 73 widened the blast radius (wrong writeKey too, not
    just ipnsName). Fix needs an in-flight generation/cancellation token on the
    active depth so a stale descent's seed is dropped once a newer nav has run;
    deferred rather than rushing a concurrency guard at ship time. Validate with
    writable-shares + shared-folder-desync e2e (add a descend-then-immediately-up
    race case).
